# Large font controls

Original controls generated by `tools/large_fonts_fixture.py` with python-docx
and explicit OOXML drawing markup. No corpus text, artwork or third-party engine
is incorporated. `native-verified.pdf` was exported from this exact `control.docx`
by the reference application through `tools/export-reference.ps1`.
`tools/record_large_fonts.py` records native text origins, red ink bounds at two
pixels per point, and SHA-256 provenance for the source and PDF.

Nine 22-inch pages cover 1, 200, 200.5, 650, bold 650, inherited 650, inactive
650-point complex-script sizing with 12-point Latin text, and retained text
frames at 1637.5 and 1638 points. The frames allow maximum-size glyphs to fit
without conflating this check with oversized body-line pagination. Frame text
remains atomic. Named-style editing in documents containing retained drawings
and active complex-script editing retain their existing restrictions.

The reference application's editing range is 1–1638 points in half-point increments. This is not a
maximum imposed by the OOXML ST_HpsMeasure schema. Native/browser page pairs
were visually inspected; 27 text lines match within 0.15pt. Browser checks also
compare all glyph bounds within 1.1pt, exercise direct editing above 200pt,
export/reopen, unrelated-part preservation, and exact undo. `body-control.docx` is generated from the same seven body pages by removing the
last two frame pages while preserving section settings and package parts. This body-only companion exercises the character-style size control and export/reopen.
